V.rationale: Visa's fundamental health and trajectory are excellent: revenue grew +17.1% YoY to $11.23B, net income +31.5% YoY to $6.02B, operating margin at 64.4%, net margin stable at 51.7%, and ROE expanded from 52.3% to 62.4%. The franchise is a dominant global payments toll-booth with structural moats. However, valuation assessment is partially blocked — PE/PB/FCF yield data are unavailable — and the stock has corrected ~15% from its 52-week high of $375.51 to $320.18, sitting at the 32nd percentile of its range, which suggests some multiple compression has occurred. The sharp OCF decline to $3.01B (−55.6% QoQ) is a cautionary flag, though likely lumpy. Regulatory overhang (CCCA, DOJ, EU/UK competition rulings) is the single largest qualitative risk, capping the score. The Q2 FY2026 earnings beat (EPS $3.31, +20% YoY, 7.1% above consensus) and the stablecoin settlement pilot with Brale (06/04/2026) provide modest near-term positive catalysts. Net: strong business with positive trajectory, likely somewhat cheaper vs history given the price correction, but regulatory risk and missing valuation data prevent a higher conviction score.
key_factors: Revenue +17.1% YoY to $11.23B in Q2 FY2026, five consecutive quarters of expansion
Net income +31.5% YoY to $6.02B with operating leverage (earnings growing faster than revenue)
Operating margin 64.4%, net margin 51.7% stable over trailing year — structural pricing power intact
ROE expanded from 52.3% to 62.4% over 12 months, reflecting genuine earnings growth and buyback-driven equity reduction
Price at $320.18, 32nd percentile of 52-week range ($293.89–$375.51), ~15% correction from highs suggests possible multiple compression
PE/PB/FCF yield data unavailable — valuation vs own history cannot be directly confirmed
Operating cash flow dropped to $3.01B (−55.6% QoQ, −35.9% YoY), OCF/NI ratio of 0.50× is unusually low
Regulatory overhang: CCCA, DOJ merchant fee accusations, UK competition ruling — targets core interchange economics
Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS $3.31 beat consensus by 7.1%; management guided low-teens revenue growth, mid-teens EPS growth for FY2026
Stablecoin settlement pilot with Brale on Canton Network (06/04/2026) — offensive move into blockchain settlement
$20B multi-year share repurchase authorized April 2026; equity declined $3.12B in one quarter from aggressive buybacks
Berkshire Hathaway full exit in Q1 2026 — portfolio rotation under new CEO, not necessarily franchise signal

sources_cited.excerpt: Visa delivered second-quarter fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.31 per share, up 20% year over year and ahead of the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 7.1%. Net revenues came in at $11.23 billion, rising 17% year over year
Visa announced a collaboration with Brale to test stablecoin settlement using the Stable Coin cryptocurrency through the Canton Network blockchain

The Credit Card Competition Act could eliminate rewards programs entirely and reduce credit access for over 100 million Americans, representing the first material legislative challenge to Visa's core economic model in decades
The board of directors authorized a new $20 billion multi-year share repurchase program in April 2026
Value-Added Services hitting 30% of revenue and growing 27%—this is a structural margin expansion story that deepens customer lock-in
